questions.text: In what John Carpenter classic is the following line said: 'I have come here to chew bubble gum and kick ass... and I'm all out of bubble gum'?
questions.funfact: The line was largely ad-libbed by wrestler-turned-actor Roddy Piper, inspired by pro wrestling promos he'd cut - it's since become one of the most quoted lines in action cinema.

questions.text: Who has just won the 2026 Women's US Open?
questions.funfact: Rybakina beat Sabalenka in New York to claim the 2026 US Open title, the same week Alexander Zverev won the men's singles.

questions.text: What does the word 'karaoke' translate to in English from Japanese?
questions.funfact: 'Kara' means 'empty' and 'oke' is a shortened form of 'okesutora' - a Japanese borrowing of the English word 'orchestra'.

questions.text: In the Tour de France, what jersey is given to the King of the Mountains?
questions.funfact: The polka dot jersey goes to the best climber, who collects points at summit finishes - the yellow jersey is the overall leader, green is the best sprinter, and white is the best rider aged 25 or under.

questions.text: Which female singer is an anagram of: LACROY SKELLKN
questions.funfact: Kelly Clarkson rose to fame as the first-ever winner of American Idol back in 2002.

questions.text: Which meat is used in the classic sandwich, a croque monsieur?
questions.funfact: A croque monsieur is a grilled ham and cheese sandwich topped with béchamel sauce - add a fried egg on top and it becomes a croque madame.

questions.text: What is Beyoncé's surname?
questions.funfact: Her full name is Beyoncé Giselle Knowles-Carter - Carter comes from her marriage to Jay-Z, whose real surname is also Carter.

questions.text: Where would you find the smallest bone in the human body?
questions.funfact: The stapes (stirrup), found in the middle ear, is the smallest bone in the body at just 2.5-3mm long. It's one of three tiny 'ossicles' - alongside the malleus (hammer) and incus (anvil) - that pass sound vibrations into the inner ear.

questions.text: Three of these flags are mostly red with one or more stars - which one doesn't fit that description?
questions.funfact: China, Morocco and Vietnam all have predominantly red flags featuring a star (or stars). Venezuela's flag is a yellow-blue-red tricolour with an arc of stars, so it's the odd one out.

questions.text: Guess the year: OpenAI was founded, 'See you again' by Charlie Puth was a huge hit, and Mad Max: Fury Road was released in cinemas.
questions.funfact: OpenAI was founded in December 2015, and Mad Max: Fury Road hit cinemas in May 2015.

questions.text: What does the DC stand for in Washington DC?
questions.funfact: The 'Columbia' part is a poetic, now largely retired name for the United States itself, honouring Christopher Columbus.

questions.text: Finish this old fashioned idiom or saying - 'Quit jivin' me…'
questions.funfact: 'Jivin'' here means kidding or fooling around, and 'turkey' has been American slang for a foolish or inept person since the mid-20th century.

questions.text: True or False: has liquid water ever been found on Mars?
questions.funfact: NASA announced on 28 September 2015 that data from the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter provided the strongest evidence yet for intermittent, present-day liquid salty brines flowing down warm Martian slopes.

questions.text: Where in the world was the original Kokoda Trail?
questions.funfact: The Kokoda Trail is a single-file track through the Owen Stanley Range, made famous by the brutal WWII campaign fought there between Australian and Japanese forces in 1942. It is 138km distance that is still completed today in memory of the trek veterans had previously completed

questions.text: Roald Dahl is known for his wonderful children's books, many of which have been adapted for TV and film. Name 5 of Roald Dahl's works that have been adapted for the big screen since the year 2000.
questions.funfact: Fantastic Mr. Fox (2009), Charlie and the Chocolate Factory (2005) and The BFG (2016) were all directed by different acclaimed filmmakers - Wes Anderson, Tim Burton and Steven Spielberg respectively.

questions.text: What do you call a sixty-fourth note in sheet music in Commonwealth countries?
questions.funfact: A quaver is an eighth note. Semi-, demi- and hemi- each mean 'half', so stacking them halves the value each time: semiquaver (1/16), demisemiquaver (1/32), and hemidemisemiquaver (1/64).

questions.text: Complete the next 5 lyrics: 'It's a little bit funny, this feeling inside / I'm not one of...'
questions.funfact: This is the opening line of Elton John's 'Your Song' (1970), written with lyricist Bernie Taupin - Elton has said he wrote the melody in under 20 minutes.

questions.text: What unusual shape is a goat's pupil?
questions.funfact: Goats (along with sheep and other grazing animals) have horizontal rectangular pupils, giving them a wide, panoramic field of view to spot predators while grazing with their heads down.

questions.text: What country is Kia from?
questions.funfact: Kia is South Korea's oldest surviving car manufacturer, founded in 1944 - it started out making steel tubing and bicycle parts before moving into motorcycles and eventually cars.

questions.text: Cerulean, Vermillion, Cinnabar, Carmine - one of these colours isn't a shade of red. Which one?
questions.funfact: Cerulean is a shade of sky blue - the other three are all deep shades of red.

questions.text: In chess notation, what letter is used to denote the Knight?
questions.funfact: N is used for the Knight because K is already taken by the King - every other piece (Q, R, B) uses its own first letter.

questions.text: What word can go before 'able' and 'mark', and after 'hand' and 'play', to make 4 new words?
questions.funfact: Bookable, bookmark, handbook and playbook.

questions.text: In Mario Kart, what do you call a small Koopa wearing goggles who stays airborne on a smiling white cloud and picks you up if you drop off the track?
questions.funfact: In Japan, Lakitu is called Jugem, a reference to a famous comic storytelling tale about a boy given an absurdly long name meaning 'limitless life'.

questions.text: Which is the older dinosaur: T-Rex or Stegosaurus?
questions.funfact: Stegosaurus lived during the late Jurassic period, roughly 150-155 million years ago, while T-Rex lived much later in the late Cretaceous, about 66-68 million years ago - T-Rex actually lived closer in time to us than to Stegosaurus.

questions.text: What number can you remove 2 letters from to get a number that's one less, then remove 1 more letter to get back to the original number's value? (Hint: Think Roman Numerals!)
questions.funfact: FIVE, minus the F and E, leaves IV - the Roman numeral for 4, one less than 5. Remove the I from IV and you're left with just V - the Roman numeral for 5, back to the original value!
